dispersion-survivorship.alt: Left: three square plots of the same area, each with 16 individuals. Clumped: three tight groups, from patchy food or living in groups. Uniform: an even grid, from territories or neighbors keeping apart. Random: scattered with no pattern. Right: survivorship curves, survivors per 1,000 born on a log scale against age as a percent of the maximum life span. Type I stays near 1,000 until late in life, then drops steeply (humans, elephants). Type II is a straight line from 1,000 to 1: the same fraction dies at every age (many songbirds, lizards). Type III drops steeply at the youngest ages and then declines slowly (oysters, most fish, many plants).
